walkthrough: Goal: make the pen's side buttons do what I want (erase or pick a colour while held, undo, redo, switch between brush and eraser), keep the colours I use in a palette and type a colour as #RRGGBB; all of it is there again after reopening.
Entry: open OpenPaint on the tablet (2880 x 1800, landscape) on an empty library and draw a black wave with the pen on Layer 1.

Erase while held: hold the first side button and draw across the wave. Where the pen goes the wave is erased (the Eraser button carries the ring while the button is down); let go of the button and the brush is back, as before.

Hex: tap the colour button. The panel's header holds a field showing the colour as #000000. Tap it, type #D03020 and press Done on the keyboard: the colour button and the wheel turn that red. Type #12345 and Done: a quieter line says Type a colour as #RRGGBB, and the colour stays red.

Palette: under the recent colours the Palette row says Tap + to keep the colour here. Tap +: a red swatch appears. Draw a line with the pen: it is red (the panel closes as the pen lands on the canvas). Type #000000 in the field and tap + again: black joins the palette after red.

Pick while held: hold the second side button and touch the red line once: the loupe shows red, and on the lift red is the colour; let go of the button and draw: the new line is red. Tap a swatch: its colour is the colour.
Remove: in the colour panel tap Edit (it reads Done now, and a line says Tap a colour to remove it), tap the black swatch: it goes. Tap Done.

Buttons: Actions > Pen buttons (its row says Eraser · Eyedropper) shows the page in the panel's place: Side button 1 and Side button 2 each with Nothing, Eraser, Eyedropper, Undo, Redo and Switch tool as words in two columns, the one they do in the ink pill, and the eraser end, which always erases. Tap Undo under Side button 1. Hovering, press the first button: the last line goes (one undo); keep it pressed: nothing more; release and press again: one more undo. Back returns to Actions.
Eraser end: turn the pen round and draw: it erases with the eraser's brush; turn it back: the brush draws.

Failure and cancel: a button pressed while drawing acts when the pen lifts, so a stroke is never cut in two; a button the pen does not have does nothing. Undo: erasing and picking are strokes and colours as ever (erasing undoes like any stroke; colours, the palette and the buttons are settings, never undo steps).
Reopen: leave and come back: the canvas, the palette (red) and the buttons (Undo) are as left.
